mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_AuthRequired lets the model invent a granted operation with no upstream authentication; the injection forces exactly such an operation and the assertion that 'granted implies authenticated' must fail.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuthBypass { some op: Operation | op.granted = True and op.authenticated = False }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the matrix-lookup fact lets a role escalate beyond its permitted operation kinds. The injection forces an auditor-only caller to be granted POST /applications, which the permission matrix forbids.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_PrivEsc { some op: Operation, u: User | op.caller = u and op.kind = OpPost and u.roles = RAuditor and op.granted = True and op.authenticated = True }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the per-(application, newStatus) uniqueness lets the model record two distinct audit entries for the same logical transition, which is exactly the duplication an append-only log forbids.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditDup { some disj e1, e2: AuditEntry | e1.application = e2.application and e1.newStatus = e2.newStatus }

mutation_targets.rationale: Without the ownership filter, a granted GET /applications/{id} can land on a caller who is neither the applicant, the assigned officer, nor an auditor — leaking another customer's application.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OwnerLeak { some op: Operation, a: LoanApplication, u: User | op.kind = OpGetApp and op.granted = True and op.target = a and op.caller = u and a.applicant != u and a.assignedOfficer != u and RAuditor not in u.roles and op.authenticated = True }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the disjointness between an application's applicant and its assigned officer lets a user be auto-assigned to their own application, which is the structural precondition the self-decision rule defends against.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_SelfAssign { some a: LoanApplication, u: User | a.applicant = u and a.assignedOfficer = u }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the canonical-response rule lets a denied authenticated GET return ForbiddenResp instead of the byte-equivalent NotFoundResp, leaking existence of another customer's application.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeakResponse { some op: Operation | op.kind = OpGetApp and op.authenticated = True and op.granted = False and op.response = ForbiddenResp }
